source.title: Fantasy Football: How to evaluate post-hype sleepers and identifying upside players the market has left behind for 2026
source.author: Chris Allen

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: Allen sees Murray's QB16 cost as an appealing post-hype bet with QB1 upside.
takeaways.rationale: Murray brings mobility, better pressure avoidance than Minnesota had in 2025, and a Kevin O'Connell offense designed to create efficient opportunities.
risks: His recent passing efficiency has not been elite
Minnesota has already endured offensive-line and quarterback instability

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: Allen lists Mayfield as another post-hype quarterback candidate worth considering at a discount.
takeaways.rationale: He fits the article's discounted-quarterback framework after prior demonstrated production.
risks: The article provides less player-specific support than it does for Kyler Murray

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: Allen is willing to buy Irving again at a lower price after an injury-disrupted down season.
takeaways.rationale: Irving retained the lead role, previously showed strong rushing and receiving ability, and should benefit if Tampa Bay's health and offensive line improve.
risks: Kenneth Gainwell threatens receiving and short-yardage work

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: Allen lists Hubbard as another discounted running back who fits the post-hype framework.
takeaways.rationale: He is presented as a candidate whose prior ability may remain useful at a reduced market price.
risks: The article provides less player-specific support than it does for Bucky Irving

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: Allen believes Evans' past profile and new San Francisco setting give him post-hype rebound potential.
takeaways.rationale: Evans retained high-end usage before injury, and Brock Purdy plus Kyle Shanahan offer a setting that can convert that role into touchdowns and efficient production.
risks: Injury and age create a meaningful downside case

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: Allen lists Worthy as another receiver with post-hype upside at a reduced price.
takeaways.rationale: He fits the article's framework of talented receivers whose market cost fell after outside circumstances reduced production.
risks: The article provides less player-specific support than it does for Mike Evans

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: Allen sees Hockenson as a rebound candidate who should benefit materially from Kyler Murray's arrival.
takeaways.rationale: Murray has historically targeted tight ends at a high rate, while Hockenson's recent decline followed ACL recovery and poor quarterback conditions.
risks: Hockenson's target share and efficiency have declined for multiple seasons
The rebound depends partly on Minnesota's quarterback transition

takeaways.label: sleeper
takeaways.summary: Allen lists Njoku as another tight end who fits the post-hype rebound framework.
takeaways.rationale: He is presented as an athletic receiver whose discounted ecosystem could improve after a down year.
risks: The article provides less player-specific support than it does for T.J. Hockenson
